38487-the-critical-game.title: The Critical Game
38487-the-critical-game.creator: John Macy
38487-the-critical-game.description: A book by John Macy. That is, it must possess some of the many merits that can be found in any type of literature; it must in some way be good writing. There is no other sound principle to be discovered in the treatises on the art of criticism or in fine examples of the art.

67202-john-greenleaf-whittier-a-sketch-o.title: John Greenleaf Whittier A Sketch Of His Life With Selected P
67202-john-greenleaf-whittier-a-sketch-o.creator: Unknown
67202-john-greenleaf-whittier-a-sketch-o.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. _The frontispiece portrait of Whittier is from a miniature by Porter, painted about 1838. The portrait which faces page 36 is from an ambrotype taken about 1857. Both the miniature and ambrotype are in the possession of Samuel T. Pickard, Amesbury, Mass._

arxiv-1801-05400.title: Structure and Evolution of Indian Physics Co-authorship Networks
arxiv-1801-05400.creator: Chakresh Kumar Singh, Shivakumar Jolad
arxiv-1801-05400.description: Abstract We trace the evolution of Indian physics community from 1919-2013 by analyzing the co-authorship network constructed from papers published by authors in India in American Physical Society (APS) journals. We make inferences on India’s contribution to different branches of Physics and identify the most influential Indian physicists at different time periods.

arxiv-1904-02751.title: Sub-GeV Atmospheric Neutrinos and CP-Violation in DUNE Preprint: FERMILAB-PUB-19-136-T, NUHEP-TH/19-03
arxiv-1904-02751.creator: Kevin J. Kelly, Pedro A. N. Machado, Ivan Martinez-Soler, Stephen J. Parke, Yuber F. Perez-Gonzalez
arxiv-1904-02751.description: Abstract We propose to use the unique event topology and reconstruction capabilities of liquid argon time projection chambers to study sub-GeV atmospheric neutrinos. The detection of low energy recoiled protons in DUNE allows for a determination of the leptonic C ​ P CP -violating phase independent from the accelerator neutrino measurement.

arxiv-2011-14149.title: Random quantum graphs
arxiv-2011-14149.creator: Alexandru Chirvasitu, Mateusz Wasilewski
arxiv-2011-14149.description: Abstract We prove a number of results to the effect that generic quantum graphs (defined via operator systems as in the work of Duan-Severini-Winter / Weaver) have few symmetries: for a Zariski-dense open set of tuples ( X 1 , ⋯ , X d ) (X_{1},\cdots,X_{d}) of traceless self-adjoint operators in the n × n n\times n matrix algebra the

arxiv-2102-10870.title: Earthquake Nucleation along Faults with Heterogeneous Weakening Rate
arxiv-2102-10870.description: Abstract The transition from quasi-static slip growth to dynamic rupture propagation constitutes one possible scenario to describe earthquake nucleation. If this transition is rather well understood for homogeneous faults, how the friction properties of multiscale asperities may influence the overall stability of seismogenic faults remains largely unclear.

arxiv-2110-05929.title: One Timestep is all you need: Training Spiking Neural Networks with Ultra Low Latency
arxiv-2110-05929.creator: Sayeed Shafayet Chowdhury, Nitin Rathi & Kaushik Roy
arxiv-2110-05929.description: Abstract Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) are energy efficient alternatives to commonly used deep neural networks (DNNs). Through event-driven information processing, SNNs can reduce the expensive compute requirements of DNNs considerably, while achieving comparable performance. However, high inference latency is a significant hindrance to the edge deployment of deep SNNs.

arxiv-2204-02168.title: A direct proof of the irrationality of tan 2 ⁡ ( r ​ π ) \tan^{2}(r\pi)
arxiv-2204-02168.creator: Lionel Ponton
arxiv-2204-02168.description: Abstract Given a rational number r r such that 2 ​ r 2r is not an integer, we prove that tan 2 ⁡ ( r ​ π ) \tan^{2}(r\pi) is irrational unless it is equal to 0 0 , 1 1 , 3 3 or 1 3 \frac{1}{3} , using only basic trigonometry and the Rational Root Theorem.

arxiv-2204-03660.title: The Bottom-Up EFT: Complete UV Resonances of the SMEFT Operators
arxiv-2204-03660.creator: Hao-Lin Li
arxiv-2204-03660.description: Abstract The standard model effective field theory (SMEFT) provides systematic parameterization of all possible new physics above the electroweak scale. According to the amplitude-operator correspondence, an effective operator can be decomposed into a linear combination of several j-basis operators, which correspond to local amplitudes carrying certain spin and gauge quantum numbers in a particular scattering channel.

arxiv-2209-10009.title: Elucidating the finite temperature quasiparticle random phase approximation
arxiv-2209-10009.creator: E. M. Ney, A. Ravlić, J. Engel, N. Paar
arxiv-2209-10009.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by E. M. Ney, A. Ravlić, J. Engel, N. Paar. In numerous astrophysical scenarios, such as core-collapse supernovae and neutron star mergers, as in well as heavy-ion collision experiments, transitions between thermally populated nuclear excited states have been shown to play an important role. Due to its simplicity and excellent extrapolation ability, the finite-temperature quasiparticle random phase approximation (FT-QRPA) presents itself as an efficient method to study the properties of hot nuclei.

arxiv-2307-10107.title: Dynamic constant time parallel graph algorithms with sub-linear work
arxiv-2307-10107.creator: Jonas Schmidt, Thomas Schwentick
arxiv-2307-10107.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jonas Schmidt, Thomas Schwentick. The paper proposes dynamic parallel algorithms for connectivity and bipartiteness of undirected graphs that require constant time and 𝒪 ⁡ ( n 1 / 2 + ϵ ) \mathcal{O}(n^{1/2+\epsilon}) work on the CRCW PRAM model. The work of these algorithms almost matches the work of the 𝒪 ⁡ ( log ⁡ n ) \mathcal{O}(\log n) time algorithm for connectivity by Kopelowitz et al.

arxiv-2401-10076.title: Weak and Strong Solutions to Nonlinear SPDEs with Unbounded Noise
arxiv-2401-10076.creator: Daniel Goodair
arxiv-2401-10076.description: Abstract We introduce an extended variational framework for nonlinear SPDEs with unbounded noise, defining three different solution types of increasing strength along with criteria to establish their existence. The three notions can be understood as probabilistically and analytically weak, probabilistically strong and analytically weak, as well as probabilistically and analytically strong.

arxiv-2404-02203.title: James-Stein Estimation in Quantum Gaussian Sensing
arxiv-2404-02203.creator: Wilfred Salmon, Sergii Strelchuk, David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur
arxiv-2404-02203.description: Abstract The James-Stein estimator is a biased estimator—for a finite number of samples its expected value is not the true mean. The maximum-likelihood estimator (MLE), is unbiased and asymptotically optimal. Yet, when estimating the mean of 3 3 or more normally-distributed random variables, the James-Stein estimator has a smaller total (expected) error than the MLE.

arxiv-2503-16796.title: Finite-time scaling with two characteristic time scales: Driven critical dynamics with emergent symmetry
arxiv-2503-16796.creator: Yu-Rong Shu, Li-Ying Yang, Shuai Yin
arxiv-2503-16796.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yu-Rong Shu, Li-Ying Yang, Shuai Yin. Critical points with emergent symmetry exhibit intriguing scaling properties induced by two divergent length scales, attracting extensive investigations recently. We study the driven critical dynamics in a three-dimensional q q -state clock model, in which the ordered phase breaks the Z q Z_{q} discrete symmetry, while an emergent U ⁡ ( 1 ) U(1) symmetry appears at the critical point.

arxiv-2505-01523.title: Subset Selection for Fine-Tuning: A Utility-Diversity Balanced Approach for Mathematical Domain Adaptation
arxiv-2505-01523.creator: Madhav Kotecha, Vijendra Kumar Vaishya, Smita Gautam, Suraj Racha
arxiv-2505-01523.description: Abstract We propose a refined approach to efficiently fine-tune large language models (LLMs) on specific domains like the mathematical domain by employing a budgeted subset selection method. Our approach combines utility and diversity metrics to select the most informative and representative training examples.

europmc-pmc7542157.title: NADPH homeostasis in cancer: functions, mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
europmc-pmc7542157.creator: Ju HQ, Lin JF, Tian T, Xie D, Xu RH.
europmc-pmc7542157.description: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH) is an essential electron donor in all organisms, and provides the reducing power for anabolic reactions and redox balance. NADPH homeostasis is regulated by varied signaling pathways and several metabolic enzymes that undergo...

pmc-10613768.title: Multiomics Approach to Acromegaly: Unveiling Translational Insights for Precision Medicine
pmc-10613768.creator: Kyungwon Kim, Cheol Ryong Ku, Eun Jig Lee
pmc-10613768.description: The clinical characteristics and prognoses of acromegaly vary among patients. Assessment of current and novel predictors can lead to multilevel categorization of patients, allowing integration into new clinical guidelines and a reduction in the increased morbidity and mortality associated with acromegaly. Despite advances in the diagnosis and treatment of acromegaly, its pathophysiology remains unclear.

pmc-10671306.title: Mapping of a Stripe Rust Resistance Gene Yr72 in the Common Wheat Landraces AUS27506 and AUS27894 from the Watkins Collection
pmc-10671306.creator: Mumta Chhetri, Hanif Miah, Debbie Wong, Matthew Hayden, Urmil Bansal, Harbans Bariana, Qinghu Ma
pmc-10671306.description: Stripe rust, caused by Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici (Pst), is among the major threats to global wheat production. The common wheat landraces AUS27506 and AUS27894 displayed stripe rust resistance against several commercially prevailing Pst pathotypes. These genotypes were crossed with a stripe-rust-susceptible landrace AUS27229 to understand the inheritance of resistance and to determine the genomic location(s) of underlying gene(s).

pmc-10674811.title: Laser Ablation of Silicon Nanoparticles and Their Use in Charge-Coupled Devices for UV Light Sensing via Wavelength-Shifting Properties
pmc-10674811.creator: Algirdas Lazauskas, Dovilė Gimžauskaitė, Mindaugas Ilickas, Liutauras Marcinauskas, Mindaugas Aikas, Brigita Abakevičienė, Dmytro Volyniuk, Christophe Donnet, Marco Cannas, Sergio Battiato, Antonino Scandurra, Francesco Ruffino
pmc-10674811.description: This study explores the controlled laser ablation and corresponding properties of silicon nanoparticles (Si NP) with potential applications in ultraviolet (UV) light sensing. The size distribution of Si NPs was manipulated by adjusting the laser scanning speed during laser ablation of a silicon target in a styrene solution.

pmc-10713200.title: Challenges and opportunities in providing high-quality surgical care in Canada
pmc-10713200.creator: David Pace, Steven Quigley, Lesley Johnston
pmc-10713200.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). SummaryThe provision of surgical care in Canada requires substantial improvement. In this commentary, we use the US Institute of Medicine’s framework for assessing the quality of health care to explore system-wide challenges that affect surgical outcomes in Canada.

pmc-10742101.title: Highly Conductive Peroxidase-like Ce-MoS2 Nanoflowers for the Simultaneous Electrochemical Detection of Dopamine and Epinephrine
pmc-10742101.creator: Annadurai Thamilselvan, Thinh Viet Dang, Moon Il Kim
pmc-10742101.description: The accurate and simultaneous detection of neurotransmitters, such as dopamine (DA) and epinephrine (EP), is of paramount importance in clinical diagnostic fields. Herein, we developed cerium–molybdenum disulfide nanoflowers (Ce-MoS2 NFs) using a simple one-pot hydrothermal method and demonstrated that they are highly conductive and exhibit significant peroxidase-mimicking activity, which was applied for the simultaneous electrochemical detection of DA and EP.

pmc-11608497.title: Towards measuring food insecurity stigma: development and validation of the Food Insecurity Self-stigma Scale and the Food Support Experiences Scale
pmc-11608497.creator: Natalie Taylor, Emma Boyland, Paul Christiansen, Alan Southern, Charlotte A Hardman
pmc-11608497.description: BackgroundWithin high income countries, individuals experiencing food insecurity have become increasingly reliant on food support to satisfy household food needs. However, experiencing food insecurity and accessing food support are highly stigmatised, negatively impacting psychological and emotional wellbeing. Being able to quantify this stigma may contribute towards reducing these impacts.

pmc-11658834.title: Evaluation of microRNA-10a and microRNA-210 as Biomarkers in Sepsis Patients With Acute Kidney Injury
pmc-11658834.creator: Hani Susianti, Catur Suci Sutrisnani, I. P. Adi Santosa, Wahyu Febrianto, Amanda Yuanita Kusdjianto, Kevin Putro Kuwoyo, Elita Riyu
pmc-11658834.description: Background: Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (AKI) is a condition that increases in-hospital mortality and the risk of progression to CKD. The current method of detecting AKI, which relies on increased serum creatinine levels or a decrease in urine output, has low sensitivity. Early diagnosis and appropriate intervention in AKI can lead to improved patient outcomes.

pmc-11679857.title: Organic Moiety on Sn(IV) Does Matter for In Vitro Mode of Action: nBu3Sn(IV) Compounds with Carboxylato N-Functionalized 2-Quinolones Induce Anoikis-like Cell Death in A375 Cells
pmc-11679857.creator: Marijana P. Kasalović, Sanja Jelača, Dušan Dimić, Danijela Maksimović-Ivanić, Verica V. Jevtić, Sanja Mijatović, Tobias Rüffer, Goran N. Kaluđerović, Nebojša Đ. Pantelić
pmc-11679857.description: Objectives: New tributyltin(IV) complexes containing the carboxylate ligands 3-(4-methyl-2-oxoquinolin-1(2H)-yl)propanoic acid (HL1) and 2-(4-methyl-2-oxoquinolin-1(2H)-yl)acetic acid (HL2) have been synthesized. Methods: Their structures have been determined by elemental microanalysis, FT-IR and multinuclear NMR (1H, 13C and 119Sn) spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction study.

pmc-12468429.title: Survival Outcomes of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in Conjunction with Cranial Radiation for Older Adults with Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer and Synchronous Brain Metastasis
pmc-12468429.creator: Ruchira V Mahashabde, Sajjad A Bhatti, Bradley C Martin, Jacob T Painter, Mausam Patel, Analiz Rodriguez, Jun Ying, Chenghui Li
pmc-12468429.description: Simple SummaryBrain metastases are a serious complication of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that often lead to poor survival. Combining immunotherapy with brain radiation could be more effective than either treatment alone, but the optimal timing of this combination is unknown.

pmc-12816231.title: Assessment of proteomic salivary biomarkers for diagnosis of early childhood caries: a systematic review
pmc-12816231.creator: P. K. Shivaprakash, Sushmitha Dandamudi, P. Tharani, Anitha R. Sagarkar, Sunaina Shetty Yadadi, Vineet Vinay, Vijay Desai, Tarun Walia, Raghavendra M. Shetty
pmc-12816231.description: BackgroundSevere early childhood caries (s-ECC) remains a highly prevalent condition among children worldwide, posing a considerable burden in both developed and developing regions. This systematic review seeks to comprehensively identify, synthesize, and critically evaluate available evidence on salivary proteomic and peptidomic biomarkers that may aid in the diagnosis or risk assessment of ECC.

pmc-12969861.title: Association of Blood Eosinophil Counts with Expiratory Airflow Limitation: A Multi-Ethnicity Observational Study
pmc-12969861.creator: Jianbo Xue, Yukun He, Xiaojun Ma, Yixin Zhang, Wenyi Yu, Xinqian Ma, Feifei Yang, Shuming Guo, Mengtong Jin, Ran Li, Wentao Ni, Zhancheng Gao
pmc-12969861.description: PurposeWhile elevated blood eosinophil counts (BECs) are established biomarkers in asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, their impact on lung function in general populations remains less defined. This multi-ethnicity study examined BEC-lung function associations across diverse populations and employed Mendelian randomization (MR) to explore causal mechanisms.

pmc-13152956.title: Prognostic impact of micrometastases and nodal status in early and advanced oral squamous cell carcinoma
pmc-13152956.creator: Gabriel Johansson, Martin Harper Hysek, Linda Marklund, Rusana Bark, Krzysztof Piersiala
pmc-13152956.description: ObjectivesSentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) enhances staging and treatment of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) by enabling detection of micrometastases (Mi) and isolated tumour cells (ITCs). However, the prognostic significance of these microscopic tumour deposits remains unclear. This study aims to evaluate the impact of Mi, ITCs, and other nodal characteristics on survival and recurrence across all stages of OSCC.

pmc-13383996.title: The Tall and Short of It
pmc-13383996.creator: Joseph Meyer, Eric M. Isselbacher
pmc-13383996.description: Corresponding Author The absolute diameter of the ascending aorta is strongly associated with the risk of acute type A aortic dissection (ATAD).1 Despite this, most aortic events occur at diameters below current class 1 guideline thresholds for prophylactic aortic repair,2 an observation known as the “aortic size paradox.
